q:
A farmer notices that the topsoil is being washed away after heavy rain.
- (a) Name the process taking place. [1 mark]
- (b) State two causes of the problem. [2 marks]
- (c) Give two methods of controlling it. [2 marks]
a: (a) Soil erosion (sheet/water erosion) [1 mark]. (b) Heavy rainfall on bare soil; overgrazing or cultivating down slopes [2 marks]. (c) Contour ploughing/ridging; mulching or planting cover grass [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A school starts a compost heap using crop residues and kitchen waste.
- (a) Define compost. [1 mark]
- (b) State two materials that can be composted. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water is added during compost making. [2 marks]
a: (a) Decayed organic matter made from plant and kitchen wastes used as fertiliser [1 mark]. (b) Dry leaves/grass, vegetable peelings, cattle/poultry manure [2 marks]. (c) Moisture supports microorganisms (bacteria/fungi) that break down organic matter and controls heap temperature [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer grows maize and keeps cattle on the same farm.
- (a) Name the type of farming enterprise involving both crops and livestock. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two benefits of integrating crops and livestock. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how manure can support crop production. [2 marks]
a: (a) Mixed farming [1 mark]. (b) Diverse income sources; crop residues feed livestock while animal manure fertilises crops [2 marks]. (c) Animal manure adds nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and humus that improve soil structure and crop yields [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer plans to irrigate vegetables during a dry period.
- (a) Name one irrigation method. [1 mark]
- (b) State two advantages of irrigation. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain one risk of poor irrigation management. [2 marks]
a: (a) Drip irrigation / sprinkler irrigation / furrow irrigation [1 mark]. (b) Enables year-round cropping; increases crop yields during dry spells [2 marks]. (c) Over-irrigation causes waterlogging, leaching of nutrients, and root rot [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer keeps dairy cattle.
- (a) What is dairy farming? [1 mark]
- (b) State two requirements for healthy dairy cattle. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why clean water is important. [2 marks]
a: (a) Keeping cattle specifically for milk production [1 mark]. (b) Balanced nutritious feed/fodder; clean dry housing and regular dipping/vaccination [2 marks]. (c) Milk is ~87% water, so clean drinking water is essential for milk yield, digestion, and preventing disease [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A crop is attacked by insects.
- (a) Define a pest. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two methods of pest control. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why integrated pest management can be useful. [2 marks]
a: (a) Any organism (insect, mite, rodent, weed, pathogen) that damages crops or reduces yields [1 mark]. (b) Chemical spraying (pesticides); biological control / crop rotation [2 marks]. (c) Combines cultural, biological, and targeted chemical controls to reduce costs, pesticide resistance, and environmental pollution [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer wants to improve soil fertility.
- (a) Name one organic manure. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits of organic manure. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one precaution when handling manure. [1 mark]
a: (a) Kraal manure / compost / chicken droppings [1 mark]. (b) Improves soil structure and water-holding capacity; supplies slow-release nutrients cheaply [2 marks]. (c) Allow fresh manure to decompose/cure so it does not scorch seedlings, and wash hands afterwards [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer stores harvested grain for several months.
- (a) State one condition required for safe grain storage. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two storage pests or problems. [2 marks]
- (c) Give two ways of reducing storage losses. [2 marks]
a: (a) Dry grain (low moisture content ~12%) in a cool, well-ventilated, waterproof store [1 mark]. (b) Maize weevils, larger grain borer, rodents/rats, mould fungi [2 marks]. (c) Hermetic storage bags/metal silos; dusting grain with recommended grain protectant and keeping granaries clean [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A herd of cattle is grazing continuously in one small area.
- (a) Name the problem that may result. [1 mark]
- (b) State two effects of overgrazing. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest two grazing-management measures. [2 marks]
a: (a) Overgrazing [1 mark]. (b) Loss of grass cover and palatable species; soil compaction and severe soil erosion [2 marks]. (c) Rotational grazing (paddocking); matching stocking rate to carrying capacity [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer wants to reduce livestock disease.
- (a) Name one disease-prevention measure. [1 mark]
- (b) State two hygiene practices. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the value of vaccination. [2 marks]
a: (a) Vaccination / regular dipping / quarantine [1 mark]. (b) Regular cleaning and disinfection of kraals/fowl runs; providing clean feeders and water troughs [2 marks]. (c) Stimulates immunity against killer diseases (e.g., anthrax, blackleg, Newcastle disease) before outbreaks occur [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer uses a knapsack sprayer.
- (a) State one use of a knapsack sprayer. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two safety precautions. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why chemical labels must be followed. [2 marks]
a: (a) Applying liquid pesticides, herbicides, or foliar fertilisers onto crops [1 mark]. (b) Wear protective clothing (gloves, mask, goggles, boots); avoid spraying against strong wind [2 marks]. (c) Ensures correct dilution rates, safe pre-harvest intervals, and prevents poisoning or crop burn [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farm manager keeps records of sales, inputs and expenses.
- (a) Name the management practice. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits of farm records. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how records help decision-making. [2 marks]
a: (a) Farm record keeping [1 mark]. (b) Shows profit or loss clearly; helps track input usage, livestock health, and theft/losses [2 marks]. (c) Enables comparison of enterprise performance to plan future budgets, expand profitable lines, or secure bank loans [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer wants to reduce financial risk.
- (a) Define risk in farming. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of reducing risk. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the value of diversification. [2 marks]
a: (a) Uncertainty of events such as drought, pests, disease, or price drops that can cause financial loss [1 mark]. (b) Enterprise diversification; crop/livestock insurance or irrigation [2 marks]. (c) If one crop fails or drops in price, income from other crops or livestock sustains the farm [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer selects healthy seeds before planting.
- (a) State one characteristic of good seed. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two reasons for using good seed. [2 marks]
- (c) State one condition needed for germination. [1 mark]
a: (a) High germination rate / free from pest damage, weeds, and disease [1 mark]. (b) Produces uniform healthy seedlings and higher yields; prevents introducing weeds or seed-borne diseases [2 marks]. (c) Moisture (water), warmth (suitable temperature), or oxygen [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer uses crop rotation.
- (a) Define crop rotation. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how rotation can help manage pests or fertility. [2 marks]
a: (a) Growing different types of crops in a planned sequence on the same piece of land [1 mark]. (b) Controls soil-borne pests/diseases; maintains balanced soil nutrients and reduces weeds [2 marks]. (c) Legumes (e.g., groundnuts/beans) fix atmospheric nitrogen for following maize crops, while rotating hosts breaks pest life cycles [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer wants to protect a stream beside a field.
- (a) Name one source of agricultural water pollution. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of protecting the stream. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water conservation is important. [2 marks]
a: (a) Fertiliser/pesticide runoff or animal waste entering the stream [1 mark]. (b) Leave an uncultivated buffer strip/riparian vegetation; fence livestock watering troughs away from stream banks [2 marks]. (c) Fresh water is scarce and essential for drinking, irrigation, livestock, and aquatic ecosystems [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner investigates why some plants grow faster than others.
- (a) Name one factor affecting plant growth. [1 mark]
- (b) State two environmental requirements of plants. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the role of light in photosynthesis. [2 marks]
a: (a) Soil fertility / water availability / sunlight intensity / temperature [1 mark]. (b) Water and mineral salts; sunlight and carbon dioxide [2 marks]. (c) Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose (plant food) [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner observes a leaf under suitable conditions.
- (a) Name the process by which green plants make food. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two materials required. [2 marks]
- (c) State one product of the process. [1 mark]
a: (a) Photosynthesis [1 mark]. (b) Carbon dioxide and water (with sunlight & chlorophyll) [2 marks]. (c) Glucose (carbohydrates) or oxygen gas [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner measures the temperature of water before and after heating.
- (a) Name the instrument used. [1 mark]
- (b) State one safety precaution. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain what happens to particles as water is heated. [2 marks]
a: (a) Thermometer [1 mark]. (b) Handle hot water/glassware with tongs or heatproof gloves and keep faces away from steam [1 mark]. (c) Particles gain kinetic energy, move faster, and spread further apart as temperature rises until boiling [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A simple electric circuit contains a cell, wires, a switch and a lamp.
- (a) Name the energy source. [1 mark]
- (b) State the condition needed for the lamp to light. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain the function of the switch. [2 marks]
a: (a) The cell (battery) [1 mark]. (b) The circuit must be complete/closed with working cell and bulb [1 mark]. (c) Opens or closes the conducting path to turn the electric current on or off safely [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner compares transparent, translucent and opaque materials.
- (a) Define transparent. [1 mark]
- (b) Give one example of an opaque material. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain how shadows form. [2 marks]
a: (a) A material that allows almost all light to pass through clearly (e.g., clear glass) [1 mark]. (b) Wood / metal / brick wall [1 mark]. (c) Light travels in straight lines; when an opaque object blocks light, a dark shadow forms behind it [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A family wants to reduce electricity use.
- (a) State two ways of saving electricity. [2 marks]
- (b) Name one renewable energy source. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain one advantage of renewable energy. [2 marks]
a: (a) Switch off lights/appliances when not in use; use energy-saving LED bulbs or solar water heaters [2 marks]. (b) Solar energy / hydroelectricity / wind energy [1 mark]. (c) Renewable energy does not run out and produces little or no greenhouse gas pollution [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner investigates friction by moving objects over different surfaces.
- (a) Define friction. [1 mark]
- (b) State one useful effect. [1 mark]
- (c) State one harmful effect. [1 mark]
- (d) Explain how surface texture affects friction. [2 marks]
a: (a) A contact force that opposes motion between two surfaces sliding against each other [1 mark]. (b) Enables walking without slipping / car brakes to stop vehicles [1 mark]. (c) Causes wear and tear of machine parts or wastes energy as heat [1 mark]. (d) Rough surfaces create greater interlocking and higher friction than smooth or lubricated surfaces [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner studies a food chain in a grassland.
- (a) Name the producer. [1 mark]
- (b) Name one consumer. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain the direction of energy transfer. [2 marks]
a: (a) Grass / green plants [1 mark]. (b) Grasshopper / zebra / impala / lion [1 mark]. (c) Energy flows in one direction from the sun to producers, then to herbivores (primary consumers) and carnivores, with heat lost at each level [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A pond becomes polluted with waste.
- (a) Name one pollutant. [1 mark]
- (b) State two effects on organisms. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest two ways to reduce the pollution. [2 marks]
a: (a) Raw sewage / plastic litter / chemical fertilisers / oil [1 mark]. (b) Depletes dissolved oxygen killing fish; poisons aquatic animals and spreads waterborne disease [2 marks]. (c) Proper waste disposal/recycling bins; prevent effluent/chemical runoff into water bodies [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner studies the human digestive system.
- (a) Name the organ where digestion begins. [1 mark]
- (b) State one function of the stomach. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why the small intestine is important. [2 marks]
a: (a) The mouth [1 mark]. (b) Churns food with hydrochloric acid and enzymes (pepsin) to kill germs and begin protein digestion [1 mark]. (c) Completes chemical digestion and absorbs digested nutrients into the bloodstream through villi [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner investigates disease prevention.
- (a) Name one communicable disease. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of reducing transmission. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why handwashing is important. [2 marks]
a: (a) Cholera / malaria / tuberculosis / influenza / COVID-19 [1 mark]. (b) Regular handwashing with soap; safe sanitation, immunisation, or wearing masks when ill [2 marks]. (c) Removes pathogens from hands before eating or preparing food, breaking oral-faecal transmission [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner observes day and night.
- (a) Name the movement responsible for day and night. [1 mark]
- (b) State the approximate time Earth takes to complete one rotation. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why different places experience different times of day. [2 marks]
a: (a) Rotation of the Earth on its axis [1 mark]. (b) 24 hours (1 day) [1 mark]. (c) As Earth rotates, different longitudes face the Sun at different times, creating time zones around the globe [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A class investigates water changing state.
- (a) Name the change from liquid to gas. [1 mark]
- (b) Name the change from gas to liquid. [1 mark]
- (c) Give one example of each change in everyday life. [2 marks]
a: (a) Evaporation (or boiling) [1 mark]. (b) Condensation [1 mark]. (c) Evaporation: wet clothes drying on a line. Condensation: water droplets forming on a cold bottle or lid of a boiling pot [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner uses a microscope to observe a specimen.
- (a) State the purpose of a microscope. [1 mark]
- (b) Give one rule for handling it safely. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why very small structures can be studied with it. [2 marks]
a: (a) Magnifies tiny objects or cells too small to see with the naked eye [1 mark]. (b) Carry with two hands (one on arm, one under base) and clean lenses only with lens tissue [1 mark]. (c) Objective and eyepiece lenses bend light to produce a highly enlarged, detailed image of microscopic structures [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A class tests a hypothesis by changing one factor at a time.
- (a) Define hypothesis. [1 mark]
- (b) Why should other relevant conditions be controlled? [2 marks]
- (c) State one way of recording results. [1 mark]
a: (a) A testable scientific prediction/educated guess about the outcome of an experiment [1 mark]. (b) Keeping other variables constant ensures a fair test so only the factor being tested causes any observed change [2 marks]. (c) Tables, bar/line graphs, or labelled observation logs [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner finds that an iron nail rusts faster in a wet place.
- (a) Name the change taking place. [1 mark]
- (b) State two conditions that encourage rusting. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest one method of preventing rust. [1 mark]
a: (a) Rusting (oxidation of iron) [1 mark]. (b) Moisture (water) and oxygen (air) [2 marks]. (c) Painting, oiling/greasing, galvanising (zinc coating), or keeping dry [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner studies magnets.
- (a) Name one material attracted by a magnet. [1 mark]
- (b) What happens when like poles are brought together? [1 mark]
- (c) State one use of magnets. [1 mark]
a: (a) Iron / steel / nickel / cobalt [1 mark]. (b) They repel each other (N-N or S-S push apart) [1 mark]. (c) Magnetic compasses, fridge doors, electric motors, or loudspeakers [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A family wants to reduce household waste.
- (a) Define recycling. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two materials that can be recycled. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain one environmental benefit. [2 marks]
a: (a) Processing used waste materials into new usable products [1 mark]. (b) Plastic bottles, glass, paper/cardboard, aluminium/scrap metal [2 marks]. (c) Reduces landfill waste, saves raw materials/energy, and reduces litter pollution [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A school uses computers for research and presentations.
- (a) Name one input device. [1 mark]
- (b) Name one output device. [1 mark]
- (c) State one benefit of ICT in learning. [2 marks]
a: (a) Keyboard / mouse / scanner / microphone [1 mark]. (b) Monitor / printer / speaker / projector [1 mark]. (c) Enables access to interactive educational resources, e-books, typing assignments, and visual simulations [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner creates a password for an online account.
- (a) State two characteristics of a strong password. [2 marks]
- (b) Give one reason passwords should remain private. [1 mark]
- (c) State one action to take if an account is compromised. [1 mark]
a: (a) At least 8–12 characters mixing uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols; not based on name/birthdate [2 marks]. (b) Prevents unauthorised users from stealing data, deleting files, or impersonating the owner [1 mark]. (c) Immediately change the password, enable two-factor authentication, and alert a parent/teacher/IT admin [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A class stores learner information in a database.
- (a) What is a database? [1 mark]
- (b) What is a record? [1 mark]
- (c) State two benefits of organising information in a database. [2 marks]
a: (a) An organised electronic collection of related structured data stored for easy retrieval [1 mark]. (b) A complete row of related fields about one item or person (e.g., one learner) [1 mark]. (c) Fast searching/sorting; reduces paper clutter and avoids duplicate or lost records [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner prepares a presentation for a science project.
- (a) Name one presentation application. [1 mark]
- (b) State two features that can make a presentation clear. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one rule for responsible use of images or information. [1 mark]
a: (a) Microsoft PowerPoint / LibreOffice Impress / Google Slides [1 mark]. (b) Short bullet points, readable fonts, high-contrast colours, and relevant labelled images/charts [2 marks]. (c) Credit the source/author and use copyright-free or permitted materials [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
Two learners communicate using an internet-based voice call.
- (a) Name the technology generally associated with internet voice calls. [1 mark]
- (b) State one advantage. [1 mark]
- (c) Give one safety or privacy precaution. [1 mark]
a: (a) VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) / online voice calling [1 mark]. (b) Cheaper long-distance communication and allows instant group discussions with screens/audio [1 mark]. (c) Only accept calls from known trusted contacts and do not share private addresses or passwords [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A school computer has been infected by malicious software.
- (a) Name the general term for such malicious software. [1 mark]
- (b) Name one tool used to help detect it. [1 mark]
- (c) Give two safe computing practices. [2 marks]
a: (a) Malware (computer virus / worm / trojan) [1 mark]. (b) Antivirus software [1 mark]. (c) Scan USB drives before opening; avoid unknown email attachments and keep software updated [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer plants different crops in successive seasons.
- (a) Name the practice. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how it may affect soil fertility. [2 marks]
a: (a) Crop rotation [1 mark]. (b) Higher crop yields; reduces build-up of crop-specific pests and weeds [2 marks]. (c) Alternating shallow-rooted and deep-rooted crops plus nitrogen-fixing legumes restores soil nutrients [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer uses a windbreak around a field.
- (a) What is a windbreak? [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how it can reduce soil erosion. [2 marks]
a: (a) A row of trees or tall shrubs planted along field edges to block strong winds [1 mark]. (b) Protects crops from lodging/wind damage; reduces moisture loss by evaporation [2 marks]. (c) Slows wind speed near the ground so dry topsoil is not blown away [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A poultry farmer keeps laying birds.
- (a) Name one suitable housing requirement. [1 mark]
- (b) State two management practices. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why clean nesting areas are useful. [2 marks]
a: (a) Well-ventilated, predator-proof, dry house with clean litter and laying nests [1 mark]. (b) Provide layers mash and clean water daily; collect eggs frequently and vaccinate birds [2 marks]. (c) Prevents eggs from getting dirty, cracked, or pecked by hens, preserving market quality [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer keeps bees for honey.
- (a) Name the enterprise. [1 mark]
- (b) State two products obtained. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one importance to crop pollination. [1 mark]
a: (a) Apiculture (beekeeping) [1 mark]. (b) Honey and beeswax (also propolis/royal jelly) [2 marks]. (c) Bees pollinate flowering crops and fruit trees, boosting seed and fruit yields [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A farmer keeps fish in a managed pond.
- (a) Name the enterprise. [1 mark]
- (b) State two pond-management requirements. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water quality matters. [2 marks]
a: (a) Aquaculture (fish farming) [1 mark]. (b) Proper pond lining/water level, balanced fish feed, aeration, and predator netting [2 marks]. (c) Clean, well-oxygenated water prevents suffocation, ammonia poisoning, and fish diseases [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner investigates how exercise affects breathing.
- (a) Name the body system involved. [1 mark]
- (b) Describe one change during exercise. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why the change occurs. [2 marks]
a: (a) Respiratory system [1 mark]. (b) Breathing rate and depth of breathing increase [1 mark]. (c) Working muscles respire faster and need more oxygen while producing more carbon dioxide that must be exhaled [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner observes that a plant wilts after several hot days.
- (a) State one possible cause. [1 mark]
- (b) Explain the role of water in plants. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one method of reducing water loss. [1 mark]
a: (a) Lack of soil water / excessive transpiration in hot dry weather [1 mark]. (b) Keeps plant cells turgid (upright), transports mineral salts, and serves as raw material for photosynthesis [2 marks]. (c) Watering/irrigation, mulching around roots, or shading young plants [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner separates a mixture of iron filings and sand.
- (a) Name the method. [1 mark]
- (b) Explain why it works. [2 marks]
- (c) Name another separation method used for a different mixture. [1 mark]
a: (a) Magnetic separation (using a magnet) [1 mark]. (b) Iron filings are magnetic and cling to the magnet, whereas sand is non-magnetic and stays behind [2 marks]. (c) Filtration (sand and water), decanting, evaporation (salt and water), or winnowing [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner tests whether light affects plant growth.
- (a) State a suitable hypothesis. [1 mark]
- (b) Identify the variable being changed. [1 mark]
- (c) Name two variables that should be kept constant. [2 marks]
a: (a) Seedlings grown in bright light will grow taller and greener than seedlings kept in darkness [1 mark]. (b) Amount/presence of light (independent variable) [1 mark]. (c) Volume of water given, soil type, seed species/age, and temperature [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner observes a shadow at different times of day.
- (a) State what causes the shadow. [1 mark]
- (b) Describe one change in shadow length. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why the shadow changes. [2 marks]
a: (a) An opaque object blocking straight rays of sunlight [1 mark]. (b) Shadows are long in early morning and late afternoon, and shortest around midday [1 mark]. (c) As Earth rotates, the apparent angle/altitude of the Sun in the sky changes throughout the day [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A school wants to protect learners' digital privacy.
- (a) State two pieces of personal information that should be protected. [2 marks]
- (b) Give two safe online practices. [2 marks]
a: (a) Full home address, passwords/PINs, ID/birth certificate numbers, phone numbers [2 marks]. (b) Use strong private passwords; never share personal photos/details with strangers online [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner accidentally deletes a project file.
- (a) Name one method that could help recover it. [1 mark]
- (b) Explain the value of backups. [2 marks]
- (c) State one good file-management practice. [1 mark]
a: (a) Restore from Recycle Bin / Trash or from a cloud/external backup [1 mark]. (b) Backups keep safe copies on USB/external drives/cloud so work is not lost permanently due to crashes or accidental deletion [2 marks]. (c) Name files clearly inside dated subject folders and save work regularly [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A learner uses a spreadsheet to record crop yields.
- (a) Name one type of data that can be entered. [1 mark]
- (b) State one benefit of formulas. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why organised data is useful. [2 marks]
a: (a) Numeric yields (kg), crop names (text), dates, or prices [1 mark]. (b) Formulas (=SUM, =AVERAGE) calculate totals and averages automatically and update instantly when numbers change [1 mark]. (c) Organised tables make trends, comparisons, and errors easy to spot for planning [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A class uses a search engine for research.
- (a) State one way to improve search results. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two checks for information reliability. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why copying information without acknowledgement can be problematic. [2 marks]
a: (a) Use specific keywords, quotation marks for exact phrases, or add "ZIMSEC" / topic filters [1 mark]. (b) Check author/organisation credibility (e.g., .edu, .gov, textbooks) and cross-check facts across multiple sources [2 marks]. (c) Uncredited copying is plagiarism, which is dishonest and violates copyright/academic integrity [2 marks].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q:
A school holds an online video meeting with another school.
- (a) Name the technology. [1 mark]
- (b) State two requirements for a good call. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one online etiquette rule. [1 mark]
a: (a) Video conferencing [1 mark]. (b) Stable internet connection, working camera/microphone/speakers, and quiet well-lit room [2 marks]. (c) Mute microphone when not speaking / dress neatly and listen respectfully [1 mark].
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

q: SECTION A (30 marks - answer ALL questions, about 75 minutes). Question 1 (5 marks): (a) What does the term 'agriculture' mean? [1]. (b) Give any two types of farming scale practised in Zimbabwe [2]. (c) Give any one horticultural cash crop grown in Zimbabwe [1]. (d) State one way in which agriculture is important to a country's economy [1]
a: Model answer, original content in the real ZIMSEC/Ministry Grade 7 Agriculture Paper 2 structured format (not copied from any real paper). (a) Agriculture is the growing of crops and the rearing/keeping of livestock for food, income or other use. (b) Any two: subsistence farming, small-scale commercial farming, large-scale commercial farming, co-operative farming. (c) Any one: paprika, coffee, citrus fruit, flowers (any valid horticultural cash crop). (d) Any one: it earns foreign currency through exports, it creates employment, it provides food security, it supplies raw materials to industry.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (5 marks): (a) Give any two reasons why farmers add fertiliser to their soil [2]. (b) State three nutrients needed by plants in large amounts (macronutrients) [3]
a: Model answer. (a) Any two: to replace nutrients removed by previous crops, to boost plant growth and yield, to correct nutrient deficiencies shown by poor plant growth, to improve the quality of the harvest. (b) Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium (the three macronutrients needed by plants in large amounts).
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (5 marks): (a) Give any three causes of soil pollution [3]. (b) The diagram below shows a simplified water cycle. Label the processes marked A and B: Clouds form and grow heavy, then release rain that falls to the ground (process A - the falling of moisture from clouds to the ground); the sun heats water on the ground/rivers/lakes, turning it into water vapour that rises into the air (process B - water turning into vapour and rising). Name process A and process B [2]
a: Model answer. (a) Any three: dumping of rubbish/litter, chemical/pesticide spills, use of non-biodegradable plastics, improper disposal of industrial waste, over-application of agro-chemicals. (b) Process A is precipitation (rain/moisture falling from clouds to the ground). Process B is evaporation (water turning into vapour and rising into the air due to the sun's heat).
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (5 marks): A farmer is growing a crop with a tall central stem, long narrow leaves, a tassel at the top, and cobs growing partway up the stem, with fibrous roots at the base. (a)(i) Which crop is being described? [1]. (ii) What is the function of the tassel at the top of the plant? [1]. (iii) Give one function of the fibrous roots [1]. (b) In Zimbabwe, this crop is normally grown in which season? [2]

a: Model answer. (a) In a storeroom or shed, kept dry and secure. (b) Any two: hoe, spade, rake, slasher, pick, axe, sickle. (c) An inventory/equipment register (record book). (d) By regularly greasing/oiling the moving parts to reduce friction and prevent rusting.

q: SECTION B (20 marks - answer any TWO of Questions 7 to 10, about 45 minutes). Question 7 (10 marks): Choose ONE leaf vegetable crop and describe how it is grown, using the following headings. (a) Name of the crop [1]. (b) Land preparation (two steps) [2]. (c) Planting (two steps) [2]. (d) Weeding (two methods) [2]. (e) Harvesting (two steps) [2]. (f) Give one pest that attacks this crop [1]
a: Model answer, using rape as the example (any valid leaf crop is acceptable). (a) Rape. (b) Land preparation: clear the land of weeds/debris, then dig/till and level the seedbed, and apply manure/compost. (c) Planting: sow seeds thinly in rows on the prepared bed, then water the bed regularly to aid germination. (d) Weeding: hand-weeding/hoeing between rows to remove competing weeds, and applying a suitable herbicide where necessary. (e) Harvesting: pluck the outer, mature leaves individually by hand, leaving the growing point intact so the plant continues producing, then tie the leaves into bundles for market. (f) Any one: diamondback moth, aphids, cutworms.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (10 marks): Describe the production of poultry (broilers) under the following headings. (a) Name of the bird being reared [2]. (b) Care of the bird (two aspects) [4]. (c) List any two products, and any two by-products, obtained from this bird [4]

(b) Any two aspects, described: providing a well-ventilated, draught-free house with adequate lighting; maintaining good hygiene (regular cleaning of litter/bedding) to prevent disease; providing enough clean water and correctly formulated feed (starter, then grower, then finisher mash) at each growth stage; vaccinating the birds according to schedule. (c) Products: meat, eggs. By-products: manure (used as organic fertiliser), feathers (can be processed into feather meal).
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (10 marks): The diagram shows a layered compost heap, with alternating layers of plant/animal waste materials. (a) Write any three materials used to make a compost heap [3]. (b) Give one reason why the top of the compost heap should be kept moist/covered [1]. (c) State any two ways (besides composting) of increasing soil fertility [2]. (d) Name any two materials that make up soil [2]. (e) Give one visible sign of soil erosion [1]. (f) What is the importance of using compost on a farm? [1]
a: Model answer. (a) Any three: dry grass, crop residues/maize stalks, animal dung, kitchen vegetable waste, wood ash, soil. (b) Keeping the top moist helps the micro-organisms that break down the material to survive and work effectively, speeding up decomposition (drying out slows or stops decomposition). (c) Any two: applying manure, practising crop rotation, ploughing under crop residues, applying agricultural lime to correct soil acidity, applying chemical fertiliser. (d) Any two: organic matter, water, air, mineral/rock particles. (e) Any one: gullies, exposed plant roots, small pedestals of soil left standing (soil pedestals), muddy/silty runoff water after rain. (f) Compost improves soil fertility and structure cheaply and sustainably by returning organic matter and nutrients to the soil, reducing the farmer's dependence on expensive chemical fertiliser.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (10 marks): (a) Give any three reasons why agriculture is considered a business [3]. (b) The table below shows a farmer's trading record for March. Complete the table by calculating the missing values A, B and C, then find the total income (D), total expenditure (E), and the profit or loss made. INCOME: 25 trays of eggs = $150,00 | Butternuts = $70,00 | 15kg tomatoes = $45,00 | 80 heads of cabbage at 60c per head = $A | 30kg carrots = $60,00 | 40 broilers = $280,00 | 15 trays of eggs = $90,00 | 50 heads of rape at 40c per head = $B. EXPENDITURE: Chick starter mesh = $110,00 | 5 bags of grower mesh at $28,00 per bag = $C | Tomato seed = $65,00 | Fertiliser = $95,00 | Pesticides = $140,00 | Bean seed = $55,00. (i) Calculate A, B, C, total income (D) and total expenditure (E) [7 marks - 5 for the table values, allocated across the calculation]. (ii) Calculate the profit or loss made [part of the 10 marks, combined with (i)]
a: Model answer, fully verified by calculation. A = 80 heads x $0,60 = $48,00. B = 50 heads x $0,40 = $20,00. C = 5 bags x $28,00 = $140,00. Total Income (D) = 150 + 70 + 45 + 48 + 60 + 280 + 90 + 20 = $763,00. Total Expenditure (E) = 110 + 140 + 65 + 95 + 140 + 55 = $605,00. Profit = Total Income - Total Expenditure = 763 - 605 = $158,00 PROFIT. (a) Any three reasons agriculture is a business: it requires budgeting/planning of costs, it involves record-keeping of income and expenditure, it aims to make a profit, it involves buying inputs and selling produce/livestock like any other business, it can earn foreign currency through exports.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set B)

q: (5 marks): (a) Name two agents of physical (mechanical) weathering [2]. (b) What do the following terms mean: (i) soil fertility [1]; (ii) soil erosion [1]. (c) How does crop rotation improve soil fertility? [1]
a: Model answer. (a) Any two agents of physical weathering: temperature change (expansion and contraction of rocks), frost action, wind, water/rain, action of plant roots growing into cracks. (b)(i) Soil fertility is the ability of soil to supply enough nutrients, water and air to support healthy plant growth. (ii) Soil erosion is the removal/washing or blowing away of the top layer of soil by water or wind. (c) Crop rotation improves soil fertility because growing different crops (e.g. alternating legumes with cereals) in sequence prevents the depletion of the same nutrients season after season, and legume crops such as beans add nitrogen to the soil through nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set A)

q: (5 marks): (a)(i) A rain gauge recorded the following monthly rainfall: January 45mm, February 60mm, March 35mm, April 20mm. Calculate the total rainfall for these four months [2]. (ii) Which instrument is used to measure rainfall? [1]. (b) What measures should a farmer take to protect crops against hailstorm damage? [2]

(b) Any two measures: use of hail nets/covers over crops; growing crops in greenhouses or under shelter; planting hail-resistant/quick-maturing varieties; taking out crop insurance against hail damage; timing planting to avoid the season when hailstorms are most common in the area.

q: (5 marks): (a) What are pesticides? [1]. (b) Why should a farmer wear protective clothing when applying agro-chemicals? [2]. (c) What do the following colour codes on agro-chemical containers mean: (i) red [1]; (ii) blue? [1]

(b) Any two reasons: to protect the skin, eyes and lungs from direct contact with harmful chemicals; to prevent poisoning/chemical burns; to reduce the risk of the chemical being absorbed into the body and causing illness. (c)(i) Red indicates the agro-chemical is very toxic/highly poisonous/extremely dangerous, requiring the most caution. (ii) Blue indicates the agro-chemical is moderately hazardous.

q: (5 marks): (a) What is malnutrition? [1]. (b) State one function of each of the following nutrients: (i) fats [1]; (ii) vitamins [1]. (c) Give one disease caused by a lack of: (i) vitamin C [1]; (ii) protein [1]
a: Model answer. (a) Malnutrition is a condition caused by not eating a balanced diet - either eating too little of the right nutrients (undernutrition) or an unhealthy imbalance of nutrients. (b)(i) Fats provide the body with a concentrated source of energy and help absorb certain vitamins. (ii) Vitamins help protect the body against disease and keep body processes (such as vision, healing, and bone growth) working properly. (c)(i) Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy. (ii) Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor.

q: (5 marks): (a) State whether the price will be high or low in the following situations: (i) many bananas but few buyers [1]; (ii) few eggs and many buyers [1]. (b) Give one advantage of growing tomatoes under irrigation in the dry season [1]. (c) Give any two disadvantages of using very old farm machinery [2]
a: Model answer. (a)(i) The price will be LOW, because a high supply combined with low demand pushes prices down. (ii) The price will be HIGH, because a low supply combined with high demand pushes prices up. (b) Growing tomatoes under irrigation in the dry season allows the farmer to sell when there is little competition/supply from other rain-fed farmers, so the tomatoes fetch a much higher price. (c) Any two: old machinery breaks down frequently, causing delays; repair and spare parts costs are high; old machinery is often less fuel-efficient, increasing running costs; it may be less safe to operate.

q: SECTION B (20 marks - answer any TWO of questions 7 to 10, about 45 minutes). Question 7 (about 10 marks): (a) Complete a table on causes of plant damage and their control, for: (i) veld fires; (ii) pests; (iii) waterlogging [3]. (b) What are the effects of the following on crops: (i) diseases [2]; (ii) drought? [2]. (c) Describe three ways of controlling soil erosion in a crop field [3]
a: Model answer. (a)(i) Veld fires - Control: construct firebreaks/firelines around fields, avoid burning veld during the dry season, report and quickly extinguish uncontrolled fires. (ii) Pests - Control: use of pesticides, crop rotation, use of resistant varieties, biological control using natural predators. (iii) Waterlogging - Control: dig drainage channels, plant on raised ridges/beds, avoid over-irrigating. (b)(i) Diseases can stunt plant growth, reduce yield and quality of produce, and in severe cases kill the crop entirely, causing financial loss to the farmer. (ii) Drought causes wilting, poor germination, stunted growth, reduced yields, and can lead to total crop failure if prolonged. (c) Any three: contour ridging/building contour ridges along the slope; planting cover crops or grass strips to bind the soil; practising crop rotation to maintain soil structure; minimum/reduced tillage to avoid disturbing the soil surface unnecessarily; mulching to protect the soil surface from rain impact and wind.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set A)

q: (about 10-11 marks): (a) Describe five ways of preventing diseases in farm animals [5]. (b) What is an infectious disease? [1]. (c) Describe one infectious disease of farm animals under the following headings: (i) name of disease [1]; (ii) symptoms [2]; (iii) measures for controlling the disease [2]
a: Model answer. (a) Any five: regular vaccination of animals; quarantine of newly bought or sick animals before mixing them with the herd; keeping animal housing/kraals clean and well-ventilated; providing a balanced, nutritious diet to boost the animals' immunity; regular dipping/spraying to control ticks and other disease-carrying parasites; avoiding overcrowding of animals; prompt isolation and treatment of any animal showing signs of illness. (b) An infectious disease is a disease that is caused by harmful organisms (such as bacteria, viruses or parasites) and can be spread from one animal to another. (c) Example: (i) Foot and mouth disease. (ii) Symptoms: blisters/sores in the mouth and on the feet, excessive salivation/drooling, lameness, loss of appetite, fever. (iii) Control measures: quarantine and movement restrictions on affected animals, vaccination programmes, disinfecting farm equipment and vehicles, reporting outbreaks immediately to veterinary authorities.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set A)

q: (about 10 marks): (a) Describe the following: (i) afforestation [1]; (ii) deforestation [1]. (b) Describe the establishment of a woodlot under the following headings: (i) site selection [3]; (ii) planting [2]; (iii) maintenance/care of young trees [3]
a: Model answer. (a)(i) Afforestation is the planting of trees on land that did not previously have forest, to establish a new area of woodland. (ii) Deforestation is the cutting down and clearing of trees/forests, usually without adequate replanting. (b)(i) Site selection: choose land with suitable soil depth and drainage for the tree species chosen; consider proximity to a water source for watering young trees; avoid sites prone to waterlogging or severe erosion; consider accessibility for future harvesting/management. (ii) Planting: dig planting holes of an appropriate size and spacing for the species; plant during the rainy season to aid establishment; water the seedlings immediately after planting; firm the soil around the base of each seedling. (iii) Maintenance/care: regular watering during dry spells especially in the first year; weeding around young trees to reduce competition for nutrients and water; protecting seedlings from livestock and fire using fencing or firebreaks; applying mulch to conserve soil moisture; replacing any seedlings that die (beating up).
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set A)

q: (10 marks): A farmer recorded the following business activities in a season: Bought 30kg of vegetable seed for $90; Bought 8 bags of fertiliser at $25 each; Bought chemicals for $45; Sold 800 bundles of vegetables at $2 for 5 bundles; Sold 12 bags of 50kg maize at $18 each. (a) Calculate the total expenses [3]. (b) Calculate the total returns (income) [3]. (c) Calculate the profit or loss made by the farmer [2]. (d) Give two advantages of a farmer selling produce directly to consumers rather than through a middleman [2]
a: Model answer, verified by calculation. (a) Total expenses: seed $90 + fertiliser (8 x $25 = $200) + chemicals $45 = 90 + 200 + 45 = $335. (b) Total returns: vegetables - 800 bundles at $2 for every 5 bundles means 800/5 = 160 lots, so 160 x $2 = $320; maize - 12 bags x $18 = $216; Total income = 320 + 216 = $536. (c) Profit = total income - total expenses = 536 - 335 = $201 profit. (d) Any two advantages of selling directly to consumers: the farmer keeps the full/higher selling price instead of losing a share to a middleman's commission/mark-up; the farmer receives payment immediately/faster rather than waiting for a middleman to resell the goods; the farmer builds direct relationships and repeat customers; the farmer has better control over the final selling price.
p: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set A)

q: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (20 marks). Choose EITHER Question 1(a) OR Question 1(b). Spend about 1 hour on this section. Write your answer in 80-120 words. a: Original question, written in the exact real ZIMSEC 7010/2 format (Section A Composition, 20 marks, choice of 2, 80-120 words, guided by bullet points) confirmed from the real specimen paper - not copied from it. Marking guidance (based on real ZIMSEC conventions for this paper type): a suitable heading/title earns 1 mark; candidates must address the SPEECH register (spoken to an audience, e.g. 'Good morning everyone', not written as a letter or story); every bullet point should be addressed with real substance, not just mentioned in passing; good grammar, spelling and punctuation are marked throughout; candidates commonly lose marks by writing a general essay about pollution instead of addressing it AS A SPEECH to a specific audience (their own schoolmates).

q:
SECTION B - COMPREHENSION (15 marks). Spend about 45 minutes on this section. Read the passage carefully, then answer the questions that follow in full, grammatically correct sentences.

VICTORIA FALLS: THE SMOKE THAT THUNDERS

Victoria Falls is one of Zimbabwe's greatest natural treasures. Local people have long called it "Mosi-oa-Tunya," which means "the smoke that thunders," because the huge cloud of spray rising from the falls can be seen from many kilometres away, and the roar of the crashing water sounds like distant thunder.

The falls were formed over millions of years as the mighty Zambezi River wore away layers of soft rock, leaving behind a deep, narrow gorge with hard basalt walls on either side. Today, the river plunges more than one hundred metres into this gorge, creating one of the largest curtains of falling water found anywhere on Earth.

Every year, thousands of visitors from Zimbabwe and from other countries travel to see the falls. Tourism built around Victoria Falls provides jobs for many local people, who work as tour guides, hotel staff, curio sellers and boat operators. This income helps to support families and to fund the conservation of the surrounding national park.

However, the falls and the wildlife around them face growing threats. Pollution of the Zambezi River, the cutting down of nearby trees, and the effects of changing rainfall patterns all put pressure on this fragile environment. Conservationists warn that without careful management, both the beauty of the falls and the livelihoods that depend on them could be damaged.

Despite these challenges, Victoria Falls remains a proud symbol of Zimbabwe's natural heritage, drawing visitors and admiration from all over the world.

Question (a): Give a metaphor used in paragraph 1 to describe the sound of the falls.
a: Original question in the real ZIMSEC comprehension style (figurative language identification, matching the real paper's opening question type). A metaphor describes one thing AS another, directly, without 'like' or 'as' - 'the smoke that thunders' calls the spray 'smoke' outright.
p: Grade 7 English — Paper 2 (Practice Set)

Within a few months, learners were borrowing books regularly and discussing stories during break time.

q: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (Choose ONE: Question 1a OR Question 1b). 1(a) Describe a clean-up campaign that takes place in your area. In your composition, cover: who started the clean-up campaign in your area; why it was introduced; what people do on the day it takes place; who supplies the materials/equipment used (e.g. bins, rakes, gloves, masks); and why this day matters to your school or community. Write about 80-120 words, and give your composition a suitable heading.
a: This is a REAL question from the ZIMSEC Grade 7 English Paper 2, October 2022 session, reconstructed from the official Examiners' Report's marking pegs (not a fabricated practice question). Marking guidance from the real report: candidates must describe what USUALLY/REGULARLY happens (an ongoing, recurring activity), not narrate a single past event - this was the single most common error nationally, where many candidates wrote about 'a day when we did a clean-up' instead of 'what we always do when we clean up'. A suitable heading earns 1 mark. Nationally in 2022, the strongest scripts scored 14-16 out of 20, while most candidates fell in the 10-11 (satisfactory) or 5-9 (weak) range - common weaknesses were spelling errors on the words 'environment' and 'campaign' (both given in the question itself), and shallow treatment of WHY the campaign was introduced and its IMPORTANCE to the community, which most candidates barely addressed. For 'who introduced the clean-up', real candidate answers nationally ranged widely and were all accepted - Village Head, President, First Lady, School Head, and Ministry of Health were all seen; this peg was answered by virtually all candidates. Nice integration point: many candidates correctly listed real cleaning tools/materials (plastic bins, rakes, gloves, masks), which examiners noted as evidence of cross-subject integration with Agriculture.
p: Grade 7 English — Paper 2 (October 2022)

q: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (Choose ONE: Question 1a OR Question 1b). 1(b) Write a report to be read by other learners, explaining how you benefited from winning a scholarship. In your report, cover: how you got the scholarship; how you felt when you found out about it; how the scholarship has helped you and your parents; and what advice you would give to other learners. Use the correct report format (From / To / Subject / Date) and write about 80-120 words.
a: This is a REAL question from the ZIMSEC Grade 7 English Paper 2, October 2022 session, reconstructed from the official Examiners' Report's marking pegs. Marking guidance from the real report: this must be written as a REPORT (From/To/Subject/Date format, or at least a suitable heading), NOT as a letter - a common national error was candidates ending with 'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours sincerely', which is letter format and is incorrect here. Nationally, most candidates explained how they got the scholarship (usually through academic excellence, or through sport, singing, dancing or quiz competitions) and how they felt (commonly: happy, excited, or 'perplexed' - a very frequently used word by 2022 candidates). However, most candidates skipped or gave very weak answers on HOW THE SCHOLARSHIP HELPED THEIR PARENTS (the expected answer involves saving money/reducing financial burden on the family) - this peg was the weakest-answered part nationally.
p: Grade 7 English — Paper 2 (October 2022)

q: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(f): When Tafadzwa's sister said 'Break the ice, Tafadzwa!', what was she telling Tafadzwa to do?
a: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. This tests understanding of the IDIOM 'break the ice' (to be first to do something, easing the way for others), not its literal meaning. This was one of the most commonly missed questions nationally in 2022 - most candidates only wrote 'she told her to get into the water', missing the essential idea of being FIRST, and some candidates misunderstood the idiom literally, writing about breaking blocks of ice. Interesting examiner insight from the real report: the question paper's own examiners noted that this question felt MISPLACED in the sequence - since it tests a high-order idiomatic/figurative-language skill, it should have been positioned later among the comprehension questions (following Bloom's Taxonomy, from simple recall through to complex), not placed in the middle where easier recall questions surrounded it.

This was a high-order 'evaluation' question, and was by far the HARDEST question on the real 2022 national paper - fewer than 5% of candidates scored the mark, since most answers ('she wanted to have more fun') failed to show that she was ALREADY enjoying herself and simply wished it could continue, which is what the expected answer required.

q: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(k) SUMMARY (5 marks): In not more than 60 words, write a summary of what the writer and her family members did at the falls. Begin your summary from the time the writer removed her shoes, to the time they prepared to leave the place. The real exam paper supplied a specific required opening phrase for this summary (not reproduced here, as the source report quotes candidates' guidance about it without quoting the exact phrase itself) - in your own practice, begin directly with the actions, naming Tafadzwa and her family clearly, and write in the THIRD person (not first person 'I').
a: REAL verified ZIMSEC marking guidance. The real marking scheme for this question had 7 possible scoring points/actions; a maximum of 4 of these points could be credited for marks, plus a further +1 mark available for consistently good grammar. Marking rules from the real 2022 report: (1) only ACTIONS within the specified time window count (from removing shoes to preparing to leave) - do not summarise the whole passage, and candidates who summarised the whole text instead of just this window lost marks; (2) always name WHO did each action clearly (e.g. 'Tafadzwa splashed water at her sister', not a vague 'they'), since pronouns like 'they' were penalised nationally for being unclear about which family member(s) they referred to; (3) never simply copy full sentences from the passage ('wholesome lifting') - for example, writing 'I splashed the water at my sister...' instead of 'Tafadzwa splashed water at her sister...' misdirects the subject and loses marks; (4) stick to the 60-word limit - some candidates lost marks for exceeding it. The most common national error in 2022 was writing the summary in the FIRST person ('I splashed water...') instead of the required THIRD person narrative, even though summary writing in English (unlike in some indigenous languages) always requires this third-person convention. Encouragingly, 2022 candidates performed better at summary writing than the 2021 cohort (the year it was introduced to this paper), suggesting more teachers are now teaching the specific demands of English summary writing.
p: Grade 7 English — Paper 2 (October 2022)

a:
**Correct Answer (D):** God has forgiven us and expects us to forgive others too.

A central Christian teaching is that believers should forgive others just as God has forgiven them.

q: The Bible teaches that Jesus rose from the dead on the
a: Christian teaching holds that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion and burial.

a: John the Baptist said these words when he saw Jesus approaching, as recorded in the Gospel of John.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: Most religions found in Zimbabwe agree that we must
a:
**Correct Answer (C):** honour and care for our parents and elders.

p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: Among the following pairs of Jesus' disciples, who were brothers?
a: James and John, sons of Zebedee, were brothers among Jesus' twelve disciples.

a: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor who questioned Jesus and ultimately handed him over to be crucified.

q: What does the parable of the Good Samaritan teach us?
a:
**Correct Answer (B):** Showing kindness/love to everyone, even strangers

The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches that we should show kindness and compassion to anyone in need, regardless of who they are.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: African Traditional Religion teaches that
a:

q: Child neglect and abandonment would be reduced if people believed that
a: The belief that every child's life has inherent value and deserves love and care is what discourages neglect or abandonment.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: A bira/umbuyiso ceremony is held by African Traditional Religion followers mainly to
a:
**Correct Answer (A):** communicate with and honour the ancestral spirits.

A bira (or umbuyiso in Ndebele culture) is a traditional ceremony held to communicate with, honour and appease the ancestral spirits.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: David showed loyalty to his friend Jonathan by
a:
**Correct Answer (B):** caring for Jonathan's son Mephibosheth after Jonathan's death.

David honoured his covenant of friendship with Jonathan by showing kindness to Jonathan's disabled son, Mephibosheth, after Jonathan died.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: A good leader is one who
a:
**Correct Answer (C):** serves and leads by good example.

A good leader serves their followers and leads by setting a positive example, rather than ruling through fear or self-enrichment.

a:

a:

Freedom fighters gathered at designated Assembly Points during the ceasefire period ahead of the 1980 elections.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

a: The San (Bushmen) traditionally used hollowed-out ostrich egg shells as portable water containers, especially in dry desert regions.

a:

q: People who build homes on land without legal permission are called
a:
**Correct Answer (B):** squatters.

Squatters are people who occupy and build on land without legal ownership or permission.

q: Which of the following is a root crop?
a: A sweet potato is a root crop - the edible part grows underground as a swollen root, unlike cabbage (leaf), tomato (fruit) or pea (seed/pod).

q: _______ is a nutrient found mainly in body-building foods.
a: Protein is the main nutrient in body-building foods, needed for growth and repair of body tissues.

q: On a map of Zimbabwe, a town marked in the far northwest, near the Zambezi River and Zambia's border, close to a major hydro-electric dam, is most likely to be
a:
**Correct Answer (A):** Victoria Falls.

Victoria Falls is located in the far northwest of Zimbabwe, on the Zambezi River near the Zambian border, close to major hydro-electric power generation.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: Which of the following is a pair of disease vectors (animals that spread disease)?
a:
**Correct Answer (B):** Mosquitoes and tsetse flies

Mosquitoes (which spread malaria) and tsetse flies (which spread sleeping sickness) are both disease vectors - animals that transmit disease-causing organisms.
p: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

q: A rondavel (traditional round hut) is typically built using
a:

q: What type of buildings would you expect to find mostly in a residential area?
a: A residential area is mainly made up of houses/homes where people live, unlike an industrial area which has factories and warehouses.

q: Very tall multi-storey buildings commonly found in a city centre are called
a: Very tall multi-storey buildings, especially common in city centres, are called skyscrapers.

a:

Deflation refers to a general fall in prices/reduced money circulation in an economy, often linked to reduced spending and slower economic activity.

a:

a:

a: Ice is the solid state of water, formed when water freezes at or below 0 degrees Celsius.

a:
**Correct Answer (B):** evaporation.

a:

a:
**Correct Answer (D):** building firebreaks.

q: The gradual breaking down of rocks into smaller particles to eventually form soil is called
a:
**Correct Answer (A):** weathering.

a:
**Correct Answer (B):** grazers.

a:

a:

a:

q: The rotation of the Earth on its own axis causes
a:

a:
